title: They are given a pure, sealed drink.
subtitle: A drink kept closed until it reaches them
then: Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said Rahiq is one of the names of {reward}the drink of Paradise{/reward}. It is sealed, kept intact for those it was meant for.
now: The thrill of breaking the seal on something new that is truly yours. A gift box wrapped just for you. {reward}Paradise keeps its best things sealed for their owners.{/reward}
old: The good things are always taken before I get there.
new: What Allah has kept for me is sealed and waiting.
try: Give someone a small gift today, wrapped with care, and think of what Allah has wrapped for you.

title: Its last note is musk. Compete for this.
subtitle: The one race worth running
then: Ibn Abbas said Allah makes the last thing placed in it musk. Then the verse says: for this let the competitors compete. Ibn Kathir links it to {idea}"for the like of this let the workers work."{/idea} The surah began with men competing over grams.
now: You check a colleague's salary, a friend's new car, a cousin's holiday photos. {trap}Competing is natural.{/trap} {idea}The verse just points it at a better finish line.{/idea}
old: Competing with others is unhealthy and I should feel guilty about it.
new: Competing is fine. The question is what I am racing for.
try: Pick one good deed and try to beat yesterday's version of yourself at it today.

title: It is blended from Tasnim, the highest spring.
subtitle: Even the drink has ranks
then: Abu Salih and Ad-Dahhak said Tasnim is {reward}the most excellent and exalted drink of the people of Paradise{/reward}. The righteous are given a drink mixed with it.
now: You are happy with a good grade, then hear there is a distinction above it. {idea}Not envy, just a reason to reach a little higher.{/idea}
old: Just getting in is enough. I do not need to aim higher.
new: Paradise has ranks, and I am allowed to hope for the highest.
try: Add one extra voluntary act today: two rakahs, a page of Quran, or a small charity.

title: A spring the near ones drink from directly.
subtitle: The closer you are, the purer the drink
then: Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Masruq and Qatadah said those brought near will drink from Tasnim pure as they wish, while {reward}the companions of the right hand are given it mixed{/reward}.
now: At work the front-row seats go to whoever knows the boss. {idea}Here, nearness is not bought or networked.{/idea} It is built one prayer, one kindness at a time.
old: Closeness to Allah is for special people, not someone like me.
new: Nearness is earned by what I do, and the door is open to me.
try: Do one act today purely to be closer to Allah, with no other reason.

title: The guilty used to laugh at those who believed.
subtitle: Ridicule as the first weapon
then: The surah introduction says it came when Makkans had started {trap}ridiculing the Muslims in streets and assemblies{/trap}, before open persecution began. Ibn Kathir says they mocked and despised the believers.
now: You pray at work and a colleague jokes about it. A relative teases you for not drinking at the party. {idea}It stings, but laughter has never been an argument.{/idea} And check that you are never the one laughing at someone's sincerity.
old: If people laugh at what I do, maybe I am doing it wrong.
new: Being mocked for doing right says nothing about whether it is right.
try: Next time someone mocks a good habit of yours, answer kindly and keep the habit.

title: As they passed, they winked at each other.
subtitle: Contempt in a glance
then: Ibn Kathir says whenever they passed by the believers, {trap}they would wink at each other in contempt{/trap}. No words, no blows, just a shared look. Allah still put it in the Quran.
now: The eye-roll across the office when the new hire speaks. The side glance with a friend when someone in hijab walks in. {trap}A look can be a whole sentence.{/trap}
old: A look is harmless. I never said anything.
new: Even a mocking glance is a deed that gets written.
try: Catch one eye-roll or smirk before it happens today. Replace it with a neutral face.

title: They went home pleased, joking about it.
subtitle: Comfort without gratitude
then: Ibn Kathir says they returned to their families pleased, finding whatever they wanted. {trap}Yet they were not grateful for Allah's favour{/trap} and busied themselves with despising and envying the believers.
now: Dinner at home, plenty on the table, and the conversation turns to mocking someone from work or school. {idea}The verse asks what you do with your comfort.{/idea}
old: Joking about people at home is just harmless venting.
new: Comfort is a blessing to thank Allah for, not a stage for mocking others.
try: At your next family meal, steer one conversation from mockery to gratitude.

title: Seeing them, they said: these people are lost.
subtitle: The verdict passed by the mockers
then: Ibn Kathir says they called the believers misguided {trap}because they followed a religion other than their own{/trap}. Later in the surah he notes they were not misguided at all but close friends of Allah.
now: Your choice to quit a dodgy job, or marry simply, or pray on time gets called naive by people who are sure they know better. {idea}Their certainty is not proof.{/idea}
old: If everyone around me thinks I am lost, maybe I am.
new: Other people's verdict on me is not Allah's verdict.
try: Write down one good choice you made that others questioned. Thank Allah for it.

title: Nobody appointed them guardians over the believers.
subtitle: Minding someone else's record
then: Ibn Kathir says these people were not made responsible for the believers' deeds or words. {idea}So why were they so concerned with them, making them the focus of their attention?{/idea}
now: You know exactly what your cousin does wrong, what your neighbour wears, who in the group chat skipped Ramadan fasts. {trap}You were not sent as their guard.{/trap} {idea}Your own record needs the time.{/idea}
old: Someone has to keep an eye on what others are doing.
new: I am not anyone's guardian. My own deeds are my job.
try: Next time you start judging someone today, switch to one question about yourself instead.

title: Today the believers are the ones who laugh.
subtitle: The laughter changes sides
then: Ibn Kathir says this is on the Day of Judgement, {reward}as recompense for how they were laughed at{/reward}. He links it to another passage where Allah rewards a party of His servants for their patience.
now: The years you spent being the odd one out for your faith at school or work. {reward}They are not wasted. They are part of what turns into joy.{/reward}
old: Being mocked for my faith is just something I have to swallow.
new: Patience with mockery turns into joy that will not end.
try: Make a short dua today for patience with anyone who makes fun of your faith.

title: From raised couches, they look on.
subtitle: The same scene, now as reward for patience
then: Verse 23 is repeated, but here Ibn Kathir ties it to the mockery: they look at Allah {reward}as reward for bearing the false claims that they were misguided{/reward}.
now: You were the one walked past and whispered about. {reward}This verse pictures you seated, calm, and looking at the One you stayed true to.{/reward}
old: Standing firm while being mocked gets me nothing.
new: Every whisper I bore patiently is building toward that seat.
try: Stay calm the next time someone belittles you today. Picture this seat.

title: Have they not been paid for what they did?
subtitle: The scale the surah began with, balanced
then: Ibn Kathir explains the question means they surely {idea}will be paid in full, completely and perfectly{/idea}, for their mockery and contempt. The surah that began with short measure ends with Allah's full measure.
now: Before you send that sarcastic reply, or pocket the extra change, remember that every deal is settled exactly. {reward}The same exactness means your good is repaid in full too.{/reward}
old: Some people get away with it, and that is just life.
new: Allah gives everyone full measure, the measure I give included.
try: Settle one small debt or wrong today before it waits for that Day.
